items.title: [soapbar] soapbar: verify_envelope_bsp accepts an unauthenticated embedded certificate (signature forgery / authentication bypass)
items.summary: Impactverify_envelope_bsp() derived its trust anchor from the message it wasverifying. It read the X.509 certificate out of the caller-untrustedwsse:BinarySecurityToken, validated only that certificate's not-before /not-after dates, and then verified the signature against that same certificate.There was no CA-chain validation, no issuer/subject allowlist, and no pinning.A successful verify_envelope_bsp() therefore proved only that the envelope wassigned by whoever supplied the embedded certificate — never that it was signedby a trusted party. An attacker who mints their own certificate, signs aforged envelope, and embeds that certificate in the token passes verification.Any consumer that treats a successful BSP verification as authentication can beimpersonated (signature forgery / authentication bypass).verify_envelope() (which pins a caller-supplied x509_cert) was notaffected — the flaw was specific to the BSP variant whose trust anchor camefrom the message.Affected versionssoapbar < 0.13.0 (all published versions exposing verify_envelope_bsp).PatchesFixed in 0.13.0. verify_envelope_bsp now fails closed unless the calleranchors trust:trusted_certs=[...] — pin the expected signer certificate(s); the embeddedcertificate must equal one of them.ca_certs=[...] — accept certificates directly issued by trusted CA(s).With neither supplied, verification raises instead of trusting the message's owncertificate. The trust anchor is checked before the signature is relied upon.verify_cert_trust=False restores the old (insecure) behaviour explicitly.WorkaroundsBefore upgrading:Do not treat a successful verify_envelope_bsp() as authentication.Prefer verify_envelope(..., x509_cert=<pinned cert>), which pins theexpected certificate.If BSP is required, validate the embedded certificate against your own truststore before acting on the verification result.Referenceshttps://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/security/advisories/GHSA-859w-52fx-hcm6https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-64855https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/pull/71https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/commit/8daaf221c1a681e6656a580b01f89f155ad97200https://github.com/hitoshyamamoto/soapbar/releases/tag/v0.13.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-859w-52fx-hcm6
